episodes.208435: A fast-moving Quasi-Linear Convective System (QLCS) in an anomalously warm and humid mid-winter environment led to an uncommon tornado outbreak on December 28, 2025. Over a dozen mainly-weak tornadoes occurred from central Illinois to the Ohio Valley. One brief tornado occurred in central Indiana in the town of Linton. Damaging straight-line winds were also reported in several locations across central Indiana. The tornado path was surveyed by NWS Indianapolis on Monday, December 29, 2025, and determined to be of EF-1 intensity with estimated peak winds of 100 MPH.
episodes.208510: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of central Illinois during the late morning of December 28th producing localized wind damage.  Additional severe thunderstorms moved across parts of central Illinois during the afternoon producing additional wind damage and six tornadoes.  Heavy rain also caused localized flooding.
episodes.208511: Periods of heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms produced flooding across parts of far northwest Indiana on December 28th.  Storm total rainfall amounts included 3.98 inches three miles east of Portage; 3.51 inches in St. John; 3.33 inches one mile east of Schererville; 2.95 inches one mile south of Merrillville; 2.74 inches in Porter and 2.35 inches two miles north northwest of Portage.
episodes.209410: Thunderstorms along a cold front caused wind damage to trees near Pittsburg in Fayette County.
episodes.209459: An unseasonably warm and humid airmass was in place across central Illinois during the morning of December 28th characterized by temperatures and dewpoints in the lower 60s.  As a 1000mb low over southeast Iowa and its associated cold front began pushing eastward, a cluster of severe thunderstorms developed west of the Illinois River across Fulton County, then tracked eastward across portions of Tazewell and Woodford counties before eventually weakening.  This cluster of storms produced an EF-1 tornado south of Groveland in Tazewell County, as well as scattered reports of wind damage and hail up to the size of quarters.
episodes.209460: The airmass continued to destabilize across central Illinois during the afternoon of December 28th as high temperatures reached record values in the upper 60s to around 70 degrees and dewpoints hovered in the lower to middle 60s.  Thanks to the high degree of instability and shear, a line of thunderstorms rapidly formed along an advancing cold front near the I-55 corridor by early afternoon.  The storms then pushed eastward, producing 3 tornadoes and scattered damaging winds eastward to the Indiana border.  The most significant tornado was rated EF-2 and caused considerable property damage just south of Decatur in Macon County.

events.narrative: Flooding occurred across many areas in northern and central Lake County.  In Crown Point, multiple areas were flooded due to clogged storm drains.  Flooding was reported near 97th Street and Buchanan Street and South Street near Court Street.  Near Hammond, a photo showed Broadmoor Avenue closed at Manor Avenue due to flooding.  East of Griffith, street flooding was reported near 47th Avenue and Hatcher Boulevard.  Near Gary, a photo showed 4th Avenue at Hamilton Street flooded. Water was also across sidewalks and low-lying sections of yards.  In Schererville, a photo showed flooding of yards and fields along Cline Avenue near a cemetery, where the side entrance to the cemetery was inundated.  In St. John, widespread flooding occurred.  Multiple roadways had flooded sections including at Tall Grass Trail and 93rd Avenue.  The retention pond at Prairie Pond Park overflowed into nearby park land.  Poor drainage areas were flooded along Parrish Avenue near 85th Avenue with ditches full and nearing the roadway.
Power lines were blown down.
Power lines were blown down.
Power lines were blown down.

A tornado touched down along Allentown Road about 3 miles south-southwest of Groveland at 9:27 AM CST.  The tornado tracked eastward along Allentown Road, destroying two outbuildings and snapping numerous trees.  It also broke 8 power poles along Springfield Road north of its intersection with Allentown Road and caused minor roof damage further east before dissipating 2 miles south-southeast of Groveland at 9:32 AM CST.
Tree branches and power lines were blown down, causing a power outage in town.
Several power poles were snapped.

Flooding was reported in many areas including many roads in central and southern Portage flooded with 6 to 12 inches of standing water.  Many ditches and retention ponds were full and overflowing.  Willowcreek Road was flooded with several inches of standing water and multiple vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.  A photo showed Crisman Ditch at bankfull with Stone Avenue culvert at capacity.
Several utility poles were blown down.  A farm outbuilding had its roof torn off and sustained siding damage.
A shed was torn off its foundation and a swingset was twisted and demolished.  Multiple utility poles were blown down on N 2500 East Road.
Utility poles were blown down 1 to 2 miles west of Forrest.

A NWS damage survey confirmed a concentrated area of straight line winds with estimated peak winds of 80 mph occurred in and west of Forrest.  These strong winds blew off a portion of the roof of a junior high school gymnasium.  Numerous trees and utility poles were blown down.  At least one shed was damaged.
Multiple reports of street and yard flooding in Manteno were shared on social media.
Lane flooding was reported on Interstate 94 one mile east of Chesterton.  A photo showed lanes flooded near the Route 49 interchange.

A tornado with peak winds of 90 mph touched down just south of 4H Park Road on the northwest side of Pontiac and immediately moved northeast across the Motorola and Vermillion Estates Subdivisions.  The tornado caused roofing and siding damage to a number of houses, apartments and manufactured homes.  Two houses had large portions of roofing blown off, leave the attics exposed.  The tornado crossed Route 23 and produced additional siding and fascia damage to a few manufactured homes in the Redwood mobile home park before ending north of E 1830 North Road.  The tornado also damaged several trees along its path.
A large tree limb was blown down onto North Mill Street.

A storm spotter captured video of a tornado touching down in a field in far northeastern Christian County about 1 mile west-northwest of Blue Mound at 2:59 PM CST.  The tornado quickly crossed into western Macon County at 3:00 PM CST with minimal damage noted in Christian County.

This tornado crossed into far western Macon County from Christian County about 1 mile west-northwest of Blue Mound at 3:00 PM CST.  It tracked east-northeastward and remained weak until it crossed US Highway 54 and reached Elwin.  Between Elwin and Turpin, several homes sustained roof damage and numerous large trees were snapped.  The most significant tornado damage occurred along East Skyline Drive as the roofs of 8 homes were stripped off, a garage was completely destroyed and tossed to the next block, and very large trees were knocked down.  As the tornado continued east-northeastward, it caused more roof and tree damage between South Baltimore Avenue and South Mount Zion Road.  The tornado then weakened, but continued to snap tree branches and cause shingle damage to a few homes as it passed through the Long Creek area eastward to the Macon/Piatt County line.  It then tracked into western Piatt County just north of the intersection of Ocean Trail and NE County Line Road at 3:30 PM CST.
Multiple large tree limbs were blown down on the east side of Cullom.  A video shared via broadcast media showed a brief burst of strong winds blowing tree debris around.
A few tree branches were blown down.
Numerous trees were damaged.
A tree was blown down.

A tornado touched down about 3 miles east-southeast of Saybrook at 3:24 PM CST.  The tornado destroyed a large outbuilding, throwing the debris to the east-northeast.  It then quickly dissipated before reaching the Ford County line at 3:25 PM CST.

This tornado crossed into western Piatt County from Macon County just north of the intersection of Ocean Trail and NE County Line Road at 3:30 PM CST.  It was captured on video by several spotters as it progressed eastward and dissipated near State Highway 32 about 2 miles north-northwest of La Place at 3:33 PM CST.

A tornado with estimated peak winds of 80 mph touched down just southeast of the intersection of N 400 East Road and E 2900 North Road, west of Clifton.  Three utility poles were snapped as the tornado moved northeast across E 2900 North Road.  Roofing material was peeled off of a house and trees were damaged at the intersection of N 500 East Road and E 2900 North Road.  As the tornado crossed N 600 East Road and E 2950 North Road, two farm outbuildings had portions of their roofs ripped off at the same property. Additional tree damage was noted. The tornado lifted before reaching N 700 East Road.

A tornado with estimated peak winds of 85 mph touched down just southwest of the intersection of E 300 North Road and N 450 E Road.  The tornado crossed the intersection and peeled a west-facing section of metal roof eastward off an agricultural office building. While no condensation funnel was evident, eyewitnesses reported visible rotation in the clouds passing over the facility and debris from the impacted building getting lofted and swirled around in the air before being deposited in a field east of the facility where the tornado ended.  This was the only damage reported from this tornado.

A tornado with peak winds of 95 mph touched down in a field approximately two miles east of Clifton.  In the first few minutes of its lifespan, the tornado largely remained over open fields and may have briefly lifted as little damage was observed west of Route 45.  The tornado began to strengthen as it moved northeast and at the intersection of N 1600 East Road and E 3100 North Road, a sizable portion of an eastward facing roof of a house was torn off and deposited in a downstream field.  Several trees at this property were damaged including one pine tree whose top half was snapped off and tossed nearly 100 yards to the east.  At an adjacent property, a barn was shifted off of its foundation and had a portion of its roof peeled off.||As the tornado reached the Iroquois River, it tore the roof off of a garage and peeled roofing material off of a house at a property next to the river. Extensive tree damage was noted at this property and just to the east along the river, where multiple trees were uprooted and dozens of trees lost limbs.  The tornado weakened a bit east of the Iroquois River, but continued to cause tree damage as it approached and crossed N 1800 East Road.  A residence along N 1900 East Road and two additional barns along N 2000 East Road were damaged by the tornado.  The tornado lifted southwest of St. Anne, shortly after it tipped over an irrigation pivot.

A tornado with peak winds of 85 mph touched down just west of N 1300 East Road near Langan Creek, northeast of Clifton producing minor tree damage. Little to no damage was observed as the tornado moved across open farm fields on either side of Route 45.  The tornado peeled roof shingles off a house and damaged multiple farm outbuildings along N 1500 East Road, just north of E 3200 North Road.  A barn was blown off of its foundation, while a garage collapsed entirely.  The tornado lifted before reaching the Iroquois River as no damage was observed to the tree line along the river.

Storm spotters and chasers captured footage of a funnel cloud south of Martinton that lasted several minutes.  Photos and video showed that the funnel cloud was intermittently in contact with the ground as it moved northeast across open fields between N 1900 East Road and N 2400 East Road.  The last footage of the funnel cloud was captured around 15:59 CST as it dissipated east of Martinton, south of E 2800 North Road.  There was no known damage from this tornado.
A portion of a dairy barn was destroyed and the top of a tree was snapped.
Thunderstorm winds downed many limbs and at least 1 large tree near Pittsburg.
A tree was blown down near the intersection of E 2880 North Road and N 3100 East Road.
Multiple trees were blown down, two power poles were snapped, and several homes had a few shingles stripped from their roofs.

Video evidence indicated that a tornado touched down about 1 mile east-southeast of Redmon at 4:45 PM CST.  The tornado caused minor damage to an outbuilding before quickly dissipating at 4:46 PM CST.
A 64 mph thunderstorm wind gust was measured by the public.
